To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
most countries link interventions to drivers, but that this link is not always made in a clear and unambiguous way.

(1) most REDD+ readiness countries propose driver-specific interventions; (2) countries with better driver data quality are more likely to propose driver-specific interventions, and (3) the interventions proposed by the readiness countries are not limited to reducing deforestation, but include other forest-related REDD+ activities.

In summary, our research is concerned with
how countries link REDD interventions to drivers in readiness documents.
the effectiveness of REDD+ interventions, and how this is related to the quality of driver data.
how countries are linking interventions to drivers, and the implications for the monitoring of effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of driver information is crucial for the design of effective monitoring systems, and for the design of interventions to address drivers.
the quality of the data on the drivers of DD and the quality of the link between the drivers of DD with the proposed interventions is better in countries that have better quality driver data.
the quality of data on drivers is not good enough to support monitoring of the effectiveness of REDD+ interventions, and that the data that is available needs to be used in a more systematic way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
countries that are able to link their interventions to specific drivers have better data on these drivers.
countries that have better data quality on drivers of DD have more specific interventions to address them.
the readiness documents reviewed provide a solid basis for the design of monitoring systems that assess the effectiveness of interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

countries are linking their proposed REDD+ interventions with drivers of DD, which will help them to better design and monitor interventions that are effective in reducing forest carbon stock changes.
countries need to design their monitoring systems in a way that is consistent with the specific drivers of DD that are addressed by proposed interventions.
REDD+ interventions are not generic, but specific to the drivers of deforestation that countries are facing.
